days.label: Tuesday, October 20
days.note: Fresh sites all over today: Carryology, Science News, Big Think, Atlas Obscura, Humble Dollar, A Wealth of Common Sense, Motor Sport Magazine, Motorsport Week, and a map blog.

hero.alt: A man fly fishing on the Owens River at sunset with snow-capped mountains behind him
hero.caption: Owens River, dusk

items.t: The forgotten British brand that changed outdoor gear forever
items.d: The rise and fall of Karrimor, the Lancashire bike-bag shop that invented the Karrimat sleeping pad and built the packs carried up Everest in 1975, then got crushed by cheap imports. Gear history rather than a product plug. New site for this list.

items.t: This legendary mil-spec dive watch now has a permanent titanium upgrade
items.d: Marathon's GSAR, the dive watch actually issued to search-and-rescue units, finally gets a regular-production titanium case about 30 percent lighter, with tritium tubes and a 24-hour military dial. A quick look at a tool watch built for use rather than show.

items.t: These tiny snakes cartwheel to escape danger
items.d: Researchers put little Southeast Asian snakes on a lab racetrack and filmed them flinging themselves into airborne cartwheels at up to 13 km/h, which finally explains the old hoop snake legend. About 700 words, with video. New site for this list.

items.t: 7 shocking comparisons between the Universe and a human body
items.d: Ethan Siegel lines up the numbers in you (cells, atoms, daily cell turnover) against the numbers out there (stars, galaxies, cosmic structures) and the matchups are surprising. No math, roughly 8 minutes.

items.t: The history and mystery of Yemen's 'Well of Hell'
items.d: For centuries locals avoided a 367-foot sinkhole in the Yemeni desert said to be a prison for jinn, until a geologist's team rappelled to the bottom and found waterfalls, cave pearls, and a surprisingly friendly ecosystem. About 1,350 words, 6 or 7 minutes.

items.t: Life insurance
items.d: Adam Grossman uses Pacific Life's $58 million settlement over permanent life insurance marketing to make the case for plain term coverage, then walks through how to size it: mortgage balance, future tuition, a living-expense fund, and separate policies for each working spouse. A tight refresher for a high earner with young kids, about 5 minutes. New site for this list.

items.t: Is it time to rebalance your portfolio?
items.d: Ben Carlson shows how the 2020s bull market has quietly pushed a 60/40 portfolio to roughly 77/23, and argues that with high-quality bond yields above 5 percent a balanced allocation no longer needs heroic stock returns. Short and practical, about 3 minutes.
items.m: A Wealth of Common Sense, Oct 13

items.t: Why has Valtteri Bottas lost his F1 race pace? The 'million-dollar question'
items.d: Pablo Elizalde digs into why Bottas qualifies close to Cadillac teammate Sergio Perez but loses the race head-to-head 11 to 4, weighing set-up, car inconsistency, and Bottas himself without rushing to a verdict. About 5 minutes.

items.t: It's race week: 5 storylines ahead of the 2026 United States Grand Prix
items.d: Chris Medland sets up Austin, where Antonelli can clinch the title with a win if Russell and Hamilton stumble, and explains why Verstappen's winning run (he is 119 points back) has Mercedes calling his form 'very, very scary'. Also the upgrade race and Haas signing Rafael Camara. About 5 minutes.

items.t: F1 Rewind: Jenson Button completes Brawn's one pound miracle in Sao Paulo
items.d: Timely history as another title could be decided this weekend: how Ross Brawn bought the Honda team for a pound, dominated early 2009, then watched Button fight from a Q2 exit to the fifth place that sealed the championship at Interlagos. About 3 minutes. New site for this list.

items.t: The Race F1 Podcast: Christian Horner on Ferrari rumors, nearly signing Alonso, and Newey's Aston Martin
items.d: A 56 minute long-form interview with the former Red Bull boss, out days before his book lands. Edd Straw and Jon Noble get him on building Red Bull from disruptor to dynasty, why he was pushed out, his conditions for a comeback, and how the Ferrari rumors started.

items.t: Bring Back V10s: Debating your 'V10sMen' suggestions
items.d: A 36 minute bonus episode where Glenn Freeman and Matt argue over which listener-nominated V10 era cult heroes (Salo, Fisichella, Panis, Herbert) actually earn the badge. Pure 1990s and 2000s nostalgia with no race recap in sight.

items.t: Science Vs: Collagen peptides, should you take them?
items.d: Wendy Zukerman spends 35 minutes testing the influencer claims that collagen powders make you look younger and recover faster, with dermatologists and exercise physiologists explaining what actually happens to collagen once you swallow it.

items.t: Planet Money: Wanna slow down AI? These biologists can help
items.d: A 29 minute history lesson about the 1975 Asilomar meeting, when scientists voluntarily paused gene-splicing research for four days on the California coast, and whether that playbook could work again. A fun collective action puzzle told as a story.

items.t: I built a drone with only one motor
items.d: Maker Joshua Bird builds a flying drone that steers with a single motor, working through failed hub designs, timing fixes, a homemade high-speed camera, and a test stand before it finally flies. Satisfying garage engineering, with open-source CAD files if you want to poke at the design.

items.t: Gdynia and the dream of a maritime Poland
items.d: In 1920 a newly independent Poland, boxed in by Germany and the German-run Free City of Danzig, picked a fishing village and built a modernist port city from scratch in under two decades. A compact history of ambition, architecture, and the limits of a harbor in guaranteeing a country's security.

items.t: Dogs seem to agree with humans that 'bouba' is round and 'kiki' is spiky
items.d: Researchers at the University of Parma tested 70 dogs and found they looked longer at the round shape for 'bouba' and the spiky one for 'kiki', the same sound-shape instinct people have. A three minute oddity.

items.t: There are 89,603 dogs in New York City
items.d: A short post on Every Dog in New York, an interactive map built from the city's dog licensing records that shows the dominant breed and most popular names in each of 197 neighborhoods, plus the 2020 puppy spike and the end of the French Bulldog boom. Fun to poke around in for ten minutes. New site for this list.

days.label: Monday, October 19
days.note: Automated edition, with two F1 podcasts and a third F1 site added mid-morning.

items.t: Ornot's waterproof, packable new cycling jacket thought of everything
items.d: A real hands-on test, ridden in the rain from Manhattan to Queens. The stuff-sack pocket and two-way zipper are the details that win it over.

items.t: Leisure Travel Vans Wonder FX motorhome
items.d: A sub-25-foot Transit-based camper with a Murphy bed and optional AWD. One-minute daydream material.

items.t: Triplet of 'ghostly' galaxies hints at what dark matter is, and isn't
items.d: Three faint galaxies seem to have almost no dark matter, and the best explanation is an ancient collision that stripped it away. A cosmic whodunit, about 7 minutes.

items.t: Here's how freaky the universe would look if light slowed to 3 miles per hour
items.d: A short piece about a browser toy that lets you walk around a world where light moves at walking pace. Three minutes to read, then something to click on.

items.t: Portrait of a Scaphander
items.d: From the Belgica's brutal Antarctic winter of 1898 to the first underwater photographs and blind cave creatures, following the naturalist Emil Racovita. About 3,800 words.

items.t: 11 retirement planning mistakes that haunt high-earning physicians
items.d: Mid-career traps: too much pre-tax money that becomes an RMD and IRMAA problem, SEP IRA instead of a Solo 401(k) or cash balance plan, and deadlines that fall well before December.

items.t: Who got richer since 2022?
items.d: New Fed data: households over 75 gained about 38 percent while the under-35s lost ground. Maggiulli's takeaway is to give to your kids earlier. 9 minutes.

items.t: What one image can't show you about the Rwanda F1 track
items.d: Alex Wurz walks through the elevation and braking zones of the new Kigali circuit that a single render cannot convey. 6 minutes.

items.t: Toto Wolff issues reality check as Kimi Antonelli closes in on the title
items.d: Antonelli is 102 points clear and can clinch in Austin with a win and the right gap to Russell and Hamilton. Wolff doubts it happens this weekend.

items.t: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set, but not for long
items.d: Keith Collantine's stats column: 73rd win from pole leading every lap, a 27th different winning circuit, and only Madrid left to complete the set. New site for this list.

items.t: F1 Beyond the Grid: 50 years since James Hunt's dramatic title win, with Freddie Hunt
items.d: 25 minutes. Tom Clarkson and Hunt's son on the 1976 season, the Nurburgring fire, the Fuji decider, and growing up with a maverick champion for a father.

items.t: F1 Nation: F1 Explains, the grid and what happens before lights out
items.d: 41 minutes. What the mechanics and drivers actually do in the half hour before a start, with Zhou Guanyu as the guest.

items.t: Planet Money: Anatomy of a movie market
items.d: 32 minutes. Riding along with the 'King of Sundance' as he sells a slate of indie films to Netflix, Sony and Apple, with the backstories of Little Miss Sunshine and Napoleon Dynamite.

items.t: Unexplainable: What's cooler than being cool?
items.d: 29 minutes. Why quantum computers have to be chilled to near the coldest temperatures in the universe, and the race to build the refrigerators that get them there.

items.t: Today, Explained: The cost of loving your pet
items.d: 30 minutes. How our bonds with pets deepened after the pandemic, and how the bills climbed with them.

items.t: I electrified my push scooter with a power drill
items.d: A cordless drill bolted to the front wheel of a Razor scooter, with one-way bearings so it still coasts. About 10 mph and 2 miles of range. Did not save money, was worth it anyway.

items.t: World first: a southern ground hornbill gets 3D printed beak prostheses at Artis Zoo
items.d: Amsterdam's zoo and Utrecht's vets rebuilt a broken beak in two printed pieces. The bird started using it the same day.

items.t: There's never been a better time to go into math
items.d: Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown on why AI proving theorems makes math more inviting, not less. A 35 minute video, so save it for a lunch break.

items.t: Why some people mow a lawn better than others
items.d: Mow a virtual lawn as efficiently as you can, then see how your route compares with 132,000 other people and the mathematically optimal path. Oddly competitive.

hero.alt: A lone two lane highway runs straight across the Atacama Desert toward distant mountains
hero.caption: Lone desert highway

items.t: Yeti's first technical jacket should put Patagonia and The North Face on notice
items.d: The cooler company made a shell. Gear Patrol thinks it is a real contender.

items.t: Ressence Type 10 DN
items.d: A watch with no hands: oil-filled discs rotate inside each other. 100 made.

items.t: Sea monkeys show scientists how to rewrite a rule of turbulence
items.d: Brine shrimp swimming in a tank reversed the direction energy is supposed to flow in turbulent water.

items.t: Life after death?
items.d: Thousands of people answered what they think comes next. A scrolling visual essay, about 8 minutes.

items.t: Jos Verstappen was hyped like Max, until it all went wrong
items.d: The father's career, which explains a lot about the son.

items.t: Invest vs. pay off debt: what should you do with extra cash?
items.d: Listener questions on debt payoff versus investing, practice buy-ins, and account types.

items.t: 'My spirit animal is now the sloth': how real retirees withdraw money
items.d: Survey answers from retired physicians on how they actually spend down.

items.t: How Horner, Brown and Wolff made their fortunes from F1
items.d: UK company accounts, so the numbers are real. Horner's exit payment is the headline.

items.t: What Ferrari is changing with its biggest upgrade of 2026
items.d: New floor for Austin this weekend, the last big push before the 2027 car.

items.t: Chequered Flag Extra: F1 super subs and the home Grand Prix curse
items.d: Latest episode, 30 minutes. Streams free on BBC Sounds without an account.

items.t: 99% Invisible: (Not Just) Another Brick in the Wall
items.d: 28 minutes on Chicago's strange handmade bricks and why they look the way they do.

items.t: Today, Explained: Data centers fight back
items.d: 26 minutes. The PR war to make AI infrastructure likable.

items.t: Sigsaly: Churchill's top secret hotline to the President
items.d: The encrypted phone in the Cabinet War Rooms, and how it worked.

items.t: The Zelda timeline, to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake
items.d: A fan-built interactive timeline of every game. Pure nostalgia.

items.t: Going 94 mph on a skateboard, new world record
items.d: Diego Poncelet, 151.8 km/h, downhill. Watch the video before coffee.

items.t: The online Library of Babel
items.d: Every possible page of text already exists here. Search for a sentence you just wrote and it will find it.
